texts: mixed: the coincidence does get recorded, but "fell on" has no covered shape here, so the translator invented a separate falling event with Day 0 as its experiencer and dropped the equinox itself into that event's time slot, and it turned "Day 0 of Year 1" into two named individuals instead of ordinary calendar terms. A stray fall event will also collide with literal falling elsewhere in the corpus. Rewrite as "The autumn equinox took place on Day 0 of Year 1." - "took place" is the covered wording for dating an occasion, so no extra event is minted and the date attaches straight to the equinox, with nothing of the original lost.

mixed: the atoms are right for a single occasion, but the standing calendar rule is lost - "the autumn equinox" is resolved to the specific Year 1 equinox introduced in the previous sentence, so the parse says that one equinox begins moth-season rather than that every equinox does. If you mean the recurring world rule, write "Every autumn equinox begins moth-season." - that gives a rule that fires for any equinox, and the Year 1 one still inherits it.
